still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban of its kind, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

The eleven state under-12 weight-indication bans and the seven-state in-person rule for low-BMI adult prescribing are unchanged, with no state added or repealed; the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived and Congress has not reopened the permanent obesity benefit.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: 48.5% ever minus 38.2% current = 10.3% of adults who used and are off now. About 42% of current users are on a second or later course (16.0 points; share fell from 45% because ~11 points of first-time users joined), 3.5 points have cycled and are off again, so (16.0 + 3.5) / 48.5 ≈ 40.2% of ever-users have cycled; the remaining ~6.8 points stopped once and have not restarted. This fits one-year persistence near one-third on full-dose weekly/oral, ~55% on low-dose plans, ~62% on monthly MariTide (home or clinic), and restart within a year of 36–47%. Age check: 0.20×26 + 0.33×39 + 0.24×49 + 0.23×36.5 = 5.2 + 12.9 + 11.8 + 8.4 ≈ 38.2. Income thirds average ~38.3, bracketing the national figure; the bottom third rose fastest (21→32) through gray vials and Medicaid tobacco-dependence fills. 38.2% of ~276M adults ≈ 105.4M users, up ~28.7M. FICTIONAL payer mix: commercial ~12.0M (11%, down from 14.5M under employer retreat; incl. ~0.3M tobacco-dependence fills), Medicare ~16.3M (15%; incl. ~3.1M dementia-risk and ~0.3M tobacco-dependence), Medicaid ~4.2M (4%; incl. ~0.4M tobacco-dependence), legitimate cash ~47.9M (45%), imported or counterfeit ~25.0M (24%, up from 15.4M). Sum 105.4M. Cash breakdown: ~22.0M weight (incl. ~6.5M home MariTide), ~13.5M metabolic/longevity among adults without obesity, ~5.5M calm/focus, ~2.6M Reset, ~2.2M alcohol, ~2.1M nicotine (mostly off-label before the Mar 2036 approval). About 24M current users have BMI under 30 and ~8M under 25. Adult obesity ~30.5%. ~16% of adults have obesity and have never used, concentrated in the rural South, the bottom third and 65+ adults without qualifying codes. Pediatric: ~1.3% of under-18s (12–17s ~3.0%, partly gray vape-quitting among older teens); 6–11 liraglutide flat at ~0.12%. About 58% of children live in a household with a current user and ~7.5M live with a parent who regained after stopping.

access.public_coverage: Medicare reaches ~16.3M users through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) codes, plus, from Apr 2036, oral semaglutide for tobacco dependence, which Part D covers as a cessation drug because the statutory weight-loss exclusion does not apply to it. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 16.3M × ~$215 average net/month × 12 ≈ $42.1B gross Part D incretin spend before rebate true-up, up from ~$36.5B; average net drifted $225 → $215. Dementia-risk route ~3.1M × ~$225 × 12 ≈ $8.4B after the 2035 confirmatory readout widened prescribing within the label. Medicaid ~4.2M, mostly diabetes codes; 7 states still cover weight use; ~0.4M tobacco-dependence fills since April, which Medicaid must cover as a cessation agent, and most states have put a varenicline-first prior authorisation on them.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide $3–20 a month across 170+ brands; Chinese tirzepatide-analogue and 'reta' vials $20–60; Canadian generic semaglutide CAD 40–70, Brazilian BRL 140–250. India and China supply ~72% of world incretin volume. India's B2C export registration (effective Jan 2035) cut direct parcels from registered exporters but pushed volume through UAE and Malaysian transshipment.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Employer weight-management coverage fell 29% → 24% (Nov 2035) → 22% (Business Group on Health, mid-2036); monitored-track-only coverage slipped 13% → 12%, holding ~7.0M enrollees inside the ~12.0M commercial users. Coverage concentrates on diabetes, CV and now tobacco-dependence codes. ACA preventive rules require non-grandfathered plans to cover FDA-approved cessation medications, so the nicotine label reopens a narrow commercial door; PBMs answered with varenicline/NRT step therapy and 12-week duration limits. Managed decline: MariTide cash $219 → $199, now including the home monthly autoinjector (Mar 2035); Wegovy pill maintenance $179 → $169; Foundayo $139–189; injectable Wegovy/Zepbound $219–259 on TrumpRx; retatrutide $299 → $279 at all doses. Amycretin $1,249 list; bimagrumab $1,150 list, essentially commercial and Medicare Advantage supplemental only. Route mix: orals ~48%, weekly injectables ~40%, monthly MariTide ~12% (~13.0M: ~5.3M clinic tracks, ~6.5M home cash, ~1.2M other commercial/Medicare). Gray market ~25.0M incl. ~7M on 'reta' vials, served increasingly by domestic 'vial kitchens' in Houston, Miami and Phoenix that reconstitute bulk powder. LSA reimbursement of calm/Reset platform fees fell from ~19% to ~12% of large employers after the Ohio settlement.

GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance)

GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Monthly driver realised through an existing product in a new form: implants remain in phase 2 (one Intarcia-successor device entered phase 3 in 2036) and are not on the market. Amgen's sBLA for a MariTide home autoinjector, with monthly titration-free maintenance, was approved Mar 2035, and $199 cash made it the first monthly incretin most people can get without an employer clinic. Nicotine driver: Novo's phase 3 smoking/vaping cessation programme (run alongside the AUD work with mandatory neuropsychiatric monitoring) filed Feb 2035 and was approved Mar 2036, 13 months later; 12-week continuous abstinence ~32% vs ~18% placebo, below varenicline in an indirect comparison, with ~4 kg less post-quit weight gain. Its label lists anhedonia as an uncommon adverse reaction (4.1% vs 2.6%), the first incretin label to name it. Tirzepatide's dementia confirmatory trial read out Jul 2035 (HR ~0.86 for all-cause dementia), and Lilly filed the non-CVD extension Dec 2035; decision no earlier than Dec 2036, now expected Q1 2037. Novo's gambling phase 3 has not read out; topline expected 2037. No new triple agonist approved; Chinese triples still in phase 3 with no US filing. No oral matches tirzepatide. US net prices drift down 3–5% a year; brands hold ~$140–280 cash.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation on full-dose weekly and oral regimens; lower on low-dose plans and somewhat lower on monthly MariTide after titration, though post-dose nausea days are reported. Retatrutide 12 mg titration failures ~1 in 6.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; absolute cases rising with volume; no change in per-user risk.
No causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. The first EPI bellwether trial (2035) ended in a defence verdict; a second is set for 2037.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Now treated as a population problem, not a per-patient caution. Medicare hip-fracture HR ~1.3 in users 65+ after more than 2 years and ~1.45 after three or more cycles, unchanged per user, but the 65+ user base grew from ~25% to ~36.5% of that age group. The NIH normal-weight cohort's 18-month interim (2036) shows total-hip BMD −2.4% vs −0.4% in matched non-users, with lean-mass loss around 35% of weight lost, in people who started with less of both.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning (Jul 2028) retained; bimagrumab adjunct; resistance-training statements. FDA opened a class safety review in 2036 with no label change yet. Endocrine Society, AACE and the Bone Health & Osteoporosis Foundation issued joint guidance (2035) recommending baseline DXA at 65+ and repeat DXA after 2 years or a second course at any age.

safety_ledger.effect: Population-level hip fracture and sarcopenia burden in older and long-term users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: CMS and NCHS claims analyses (2036) show the age-adjusted 65+ hip-fracture rate up ~7% from 2032, ending a two-decade decline. Attributable estimate: ~19M users 65+ × ~0.5% annual baseline risk × ~0.3 excess ≈ 28,000 excess hip fractures a year, about one in eleven US hip fractures. Weighted toward women 70+, cyclers and gray-market users without DXA. Falls clinics report 'weight-loss sarcopenia' as a routine referral reason.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No new federal policy. Medicare DXA claims up ~40%. Several Medicare Advantage plans added strength-training and fall-prevention supplemental benefits, and some started routing bimagrumab through prior authorisation.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No signal in the nicotine programme despite structured neuropsychiatric monitoring modelled on varenicline's EAGLES trial.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~7–8% at weight doses vs ~3% of controls, ~10–11% on retatrutide. First randomised low-dose measurement, from the nicotine trials: 4.1% vs 2.6% on placebo. Real but uncommon at the doses calm and longevity users take, and the same trials found no focus or calm benefit separable from placebo.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed as an uncommon adverse reaction on the Mar 2036 tobacco-dependence label; not yet on weight labels; the 2034 FTC–FDA consent orders on marketing remain.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months; fastest after retatrutide 12 mg and among gray users who lose supply. ~1.5M commercial users who lost employer coverage in 2035–36 moved to cash; others stopped and regained.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins the chronic-therapy framing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron, vitamin D; fat-soluble deficiency tied to EPI; low ferritin in adolescent girls; low vitamin D now also read as a bone cofactor in older users.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~2× incidence after more than 5 years continuous semaglutide; partial recovery in about half who stop 12+ months; tirzepatide 5-year excess small and now borderline significant at 7 years.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide class labelling (2031); tirzepatide under review.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; decades-long pediatric exposure; repeated cycling; people without obesity
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~14 years of semaglutide follow-up. ~24M current users have BMI under 30. The NIH normal-weight cohort's first bone signal is above. Cycling effects on the pancreas are still poorly characterised.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric PMRs continue; NIH cohort expanded.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~71,000 by mid-2036. In Sep 2035 CDC linked reconstituted 'reta' vials from a Houston repackager to ~340 cases of nontuberculous mycobacterial abscess and sepsis in nine states, 4 deaths. Poison-centre calls ~9× 2025, mostly tenfold dosing errors from unit confusion on mg/mL vials. Counterfeit insulin-pen cases recurred at a far lower level (~120 ED visits in 2035).
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts unchanged in scope. India's B2C export registration took effect Jan 2035 and shifted routes. No new federal or state law in the window; existing state felony statutes are prosecuted sporadically.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The 48-month liraglutide PMR update (2035) shows the ~0.7 cm/year deficit persisting with partial catch-up beginning in some who stopped; Swedish ARFID HR ~1.8. Final adult height still unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label monitoring retained; eleven-state bans unchanged; EMA specialist-initiation rule unchanged.

food_and_beverage.state: About 55% of US households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~16–18% from 2025, sugary drinks ~14%. Dollar sales are roughly flat on price, protein and the longevity aisle. Calcium-, vitamin-D- and leucine-fortified 'bone-and-muscle' lines from Danone, Abbott and private label grew fastest in 2036, pitched at women 60+. Zip-code planning is standard at Walmart, Kroger and Dollar General, and Dollar General's high-density-user zips now carry protein shakes beside the snack cakes.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes are down ~20% from 2025 and beer ~13%. AUD fills (~2.2M cash plus covered) keep removing heavy drinkers. Two more regional brewers consolidated. Tobacco is the new adjacent casualty: US cigarette volumes fell ~11% in 2036 against a typical ~8–9% decline, and nicotine-pouch growth stalled, though analysts attribute less than half of the gap to incretins.

restaurants.state: Traffic is slightly down. Portion tiers are standard. QSR value menus still carry lower-income markets, and late-night traffic rises with regain after coverage losses and gray-supply gaps. Upscale steakhouses keep 'protein-forward' tasting menus.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking. 'Lifted-body' and shoulder-structured tailoring sells as a muscle signal. Resale, stretch and size-flex lines serve cyclers and people who lost coverage. Hip-protector underwear and fall-safe footwear became a visible senior category at Walgreens and Kohl's.

fitness.state: Strength training is the growth line. Premium DXA-plus-coaching runs $250–450 a month; bimagrumab-plus-coaching packages are limited to the commercially and MA-insured. Budget chains' $39 lean-mass add-ons are standard. SilverSneakers-type programmes added supervised resistance blocks under MA supplemental benefits. Longevity clinics now sell 'bone age' alongside biological age.

insurance.state: Employer weight coverage is down to 22%; employers cite pharmacy trend of ~+7% and the arrival of cheap home MariTide in cash as a reason employees 'have options'. Adherence differentials persist under the 2027 guidance at firms that still cover. The nicotine label forces cessation coverage, which PBMs manage through step therapy. Part D premiums rose again for 2036. MA plans compete on fall-prevention benefits.

pharma.state: Amgen grew fastest on home MariTide; Novo added the nicotine label; Lilly holds the dementia route and retatrutide. Litigation and counterfeit-defence spending is ~$1.3B a year across the four. Altria and PMI cite 'GLP-1 cessation effects' in guidance. Indian and Chinese makers dominate global volume.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Body shape reads as payment route, and now also as muscle. Lean and visibly muscled, with a DXA on file, means insured or rich enough for coaching and bimagrumab. Lean and soft, with thin arms, is 'mail-thin': gray vials or cash pills and no scan. A monthly autoinjector bruise on the thigh used to mean an employer clinic track and now means $199 at home. In older adults, a cane after a weight loss is read as a cash-plan body.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: In Charlotte and Austin, thinness without muscle is now slightly déclassé, and the boast is a T-score and a lean-mass percentile. Along the Columbus logistics corridor, employers that dropped coverage turned the track body into a $199 personal expense, and shift leads keep it. In Memphis and the Delta, gray 'reta' still delivers surgical losses with no scan, and the falls clinic at Methodist sees the results in women in their sixties. In Scottsdale retirement communities, strength classes are booked out and group conversation includes DXA numbers.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are shorter and protein-led. Holiday 'tasting' portions are normal in high-density zips. Church suppers in the Bread Alone network, now ~900 congregations, added calcium-fortified dishes for older members. The post-quit smoker's meal, once a weight-gain ritual, is shrinking.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: 'Lean-mass verified' remains a premium app tier, and 'bone verified' appeared on Hinge's over-50 product. Reset badges lost some cachet after the low-dose trial data. Couples still negotiate shot days, now monthly.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: In the upper tier appetite is still managed noise, and the new anxiety is about losing muscle, not weight. In lower-income communities appetite signals lost coverage or a lost package. Unmuted lost some of its target after employers retreated, and it now organises around the hip-fracture data. The MAHA wing is split over the nicotine approval: some call it a cure for smoking, others another lifetime script.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The Mar 2036 tobacco-dependence label lists anhedonia as uncommon (4.1% vs 2.6% placebo at low dose). Weight-dose rates are ~7–8% vs ~3%, and ~10–11% on retatrutide. About 5.5M calm/focus, 2.6M Reset and 13.5M longevity users are on low doses, which implies roughly 0.3M people with drug-attributable anhedonia among them, plus an unmeasured gray share. The same trials showed no calm or focus benefit separable from placebo.
interior_life.framing: Clinicians and labels now call it a side effect: uncommon, dose-related, reversible on stopping. Employers stopped calling it 'steadiness' after the Ohio settlement. Platforms still say 'balance' and do not mention mood. Unmuted calls it the side effect they were right about, though it turned out smaller than they said.
interior_life.effect_on_work: The Ohio call-centre suit settled in Oct 2035: the operator removed track enrolment from promotion criteria and paid an undisclosed sum, and two large 3PLs followed. Broker 'focus cohort' analytics were rebranded as general retention analytics and lost buyers. Clinic-administered tracks still exist at ~12% of employers, and enrolees still have fewer absences, but enrolment is no longer read as a promotion signal. Occupational health clinics now screen long-term users for low mood the same way they screen for B12.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Sportsbook handle per account in high-density states is still ~15% below 2032 but has stopped falling. Ambient and slow-game programming continues without the 'calm segment' label. 'Off' memoir has faded. A new genre of 'I quit and it was the drug' videos runs alongside 'I quit and it was me'. Stand-up has moved on from the flat audience to hip-protector jokes.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Desire mismatch is still a common complaint at couples' practices, but therapists now check the dose and the label before blaming the relationship. Some couples on shared calm plans stopped after the trial data and report more conflict and more sex.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: No legislature acted. The restriction coalition from 2034 stalled: bans already in place were left alone and none were added. The tobacco lobby and convenience-store associations quietly fund 'mail-thin' fracture messaging. Turnout claims about a sedated electorate faded with the low-dose numbers.

state.regulatory_posture: Passive. The FDA approved products on ordinary timelines (home MariTide, the oral semaglutide nicotine label) and opened a bone safety review without acting on it. No state enacted, expanded or repealed incretin laws in 2035–36, and Congress passed nothing. The existing 2034 bans, in-person rules and advertising limits still stand and are enforced unevenly.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: None new. The existing ACA preventive-services and Medicaid cessation-coverage rules, written for varenicline, now automatically cover oral semaglutide for tobacco dependence, a mandate nobody voted on in this window. The 2027 30% adherence guidance stands. TrumpRx runs on manufacturer prices.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged in law. Clinic administration, PBM fills and home-autoinjector connected-cap data flow to vendors under consent. Monthly dosing makes adherence a monthly logged event rather than a weekly choice. Employer use of that data for promotions retreated through litigation, not regulation. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE unchanged. The Army recruit oral pilot continues. DOT's 2033 guidance stands, and the nicotine label adds another disclosed, non-disqualifying use. The VA began offering oral semaglutide for tobacco dependence under its existing cessation formulary in mid-2036.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India's B2C export registration took effect Jan 2035. Registered exporters' direct parcels fell, but volume rerouted through Dubai and Port Klang, and bulk API moves to domestic vial kitchens. There is still no CBP mail agreement. Chinese 'reta' supply runs through research-peptide fronts. The US cash-to-Indian-generic gap is ~35–60×.

events.event: India's export-registration rule for consumer pharmaceutical parcels takes effect; within months, US seizures show semaglutide and 'reta' powder rerouted through Dubai and Malaysia and reconstituted in domestic repackaging operations
FDA approves an at-home monthly autoinjector for Amgen's MariTide; Amgen sets cash price at $199, and home users pass six million by mid-2036

CDC ties contaminated retatrutide-labelled vials from a Houston repackager to about 340 abscess and sepsis cases in nine states and four deaths, as the number of Americans on unapproved product approaches 25 million

Business Group on Health survey: employers covering weight-loss drugs fall from 29% to 24%, heading to 22% in 2036; weeks earlier an Ohio call-centre operator settles a promotion-bias suit and drops track enrolment from promotion criteria

FDA approves oral semaglutide to help adults quit smoking and vaping; the label is the first incretin label to list anhedonia, as an uncommon side effect seen in 4.1% of patients versus 2.6% on placebo

Medicare claims analysis finds hip fractures among Americans over 65 up about 7% since 2032, reversing a two-decade decline, with an estimated 28,000 excess fractures a year among long-term incretin users; endocrine and bone societies urge routine DXA scans

open_tensions: The tobacco-dependence label opened an unlegislated back door: ACA preventive rules, Medicaid and Part D must cover oral semaglutide for smokers just as employers retreat from weight coverage, and PBMs are holding it behind varenicline-first step therapy and 12-week limits that most users will outlast.

About 28,000 excess hip fractures a year are now attributed to long-term use in older adults, but DXA, coaching and bimagrumab reach mainly the insured and the rich; the fastest growth is among cash and gray users who are never scanned, and the FDA review has produced no label.

Roughly 25 million Americans use unapproved product, increasingly reconstituted in US vial kitchens rather than shipped finished, so India's parcel rule moved the risk onshore without reducing it, and no state or federal body acted in the window.

Lilly's non-CVD dementia filing reaches a decision in 2037; approval would put millions of 50–70-year-olds without heart disease into Medicare's incretin spend, currently ~$42B a year, through a code Congress never voted on.

prose.headline: Thin Is Cheap Now: In 2036 the status body is muscle, a bone scan and a $199 shot, and it's the hip fractures that tell you who paid
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 almost two American adults in five take an incretin drug, about a hundred and five million people, and nearly half have tried one. Employers did not drive the growth. They pulled back, from 29 percent covering weight-loss drugs to 22, on the reasoning that workers now had cheaper options. Workers did. In March 2035 Amgen began selling its monthly MariTide shot as a home autoinjector for $199 in cash, and more than six million people inject it into a thigh once a month, with no clinic, no employer and nothing to remember weekly. The pills are cheaper too: $169 for Wegovy at maintenance and $149 to start. The list price on the box is still $1,349.

The drug kept collecting reasons to take it. In March 2036 the FDA approved oral semaglutide to help adults quit cigarettes and vapes. It works less well than varenicline but costs smokers four fewer kilos of weight gain. Because federal rules already require insurers and Medicaid to cover approved quit-smoking drugs, an obesity drug that Congress never agreed to pay for is now covered, behind step therapy, for some thirty million smokers. Insurers are writing prior-authorisation forms as fast as they can.

The same label did something quieter. The cessation trials had to track mood closely, and they found that a low dose flattens pleasure in about four people in a hundred, against under three on placebo. That is real and uncommon. They also found the low dose did nothing measurable for calm or focus. The 'steadiness' that employers had been reimbursing through wellness accounts was mostly expectation. An Ohio call-centre company settled a lawsuit over promoting workers on monitored tracks, other firms quietly followed, and the anhedonia that had looked like a workplace culture went back to being a line in a leaflet.

The bones are the harder news. Older users were always warned about losing muscle. In June 2036 Medicare claims showed hip fractures among people over sixty-five rising for the first time in twenty years, with roughly twenty-eight thousand extra breaks a year attributed to long-term users, most of them women over seventy and people who had cycled on and off. Endocrinologists now tell everyone over sixty-five to get a bone scan. The scan, the coaching and the $1,150 muscle drug go mostly to people with good insurance.

That has changed what a body says. In Charlotte and Austin, being thin is no longer impressive on its own. Thinness without muscle has a name, 'mail-thin', and it means vials. The status body is lean and visibly strong, with a bone-density score that clinics now print beside biological age. In Scottsdale the strength classes are booked out. In Memphis, gray 'reta' still produces surgical-scale weight loss with no scan, and the falls clinic sees it in women in their sixties.

The mail now carries twenty-five million people's supply, up from fifteen. When India began registering consumer exports in 2035, the powder went through Dubai instead and was made up into vials in back rooms in Houston and Miami. One of those rooms sent out contaminated vials that put 340 people in hospital with abscesses and sepsis, and four died. No legislature acted. The eleven states that banned prescribing to young children left the bans in place and passed nothing new, and neither did anyone else.

Spirits are down a fifth since 2025, and cigarette volumes are falling a little faster than usual. Grocery shelves now stock calcium and leucine for women over sixty. Couples' therapists ask about the dose before they ask about the marriage. Lilly's bid to extend its dementia label to people without heart disease will be decided early next year. Approval would add millions to Medicare's $42 billion incretin bill, through a door Congress never voted to open.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Darlene Pruitt does her shot at 5:10 a.m. on the first Tuesday, sitting on the edge of the tub in Grove City, Ohio. The cap on the pen blinks green. $199, charged to the Visa, since January.

She drives to the distribution centre with the window cracked and a cigarette she promised herself would be the last of the pack. At the gate there's a laminated sign about the new benefits portal. Her badge still says TRACK on it from when the clinic down the hall did her shots for free. Nobody's taken the sticker off.

At lunch she calls the pharmacy about the smoking pill her nurse practitioner wrote. Denied: try Chantix first. She tried Chantix in 2029 and dreamt about her dead brother every night for a month. She writes 'appeal' on her hand in pen.

At three her phone buzzes. Her mother is at Mount Carmel, hip, fell reaching for the coffee filters. Her mother is eighty-one and has been on Zepbound through Medicare for four years because of her stents, and has lost forty pounds and, the surgeon says on the phone, a lot of what held her up.

Darlene sits in the parking garage and doesn't cry. She notices she doesn't, and remembers the paper in the pill box that said uncommon, and thinks that's not it, that's just Tuesday.

In the ER her mother says, 'You look good, honey. Thin.'

Darlene looks at her own wrists. She books a bone scan for herself on the app. $185, cash. First available is March.
